title: 20260713 - From Zero to Agent Building agents in Business Central

chapters.title: What is an agent and existing agents in Business Central
Requirements and setup for building custom agents
Creating a custom agent - configuration and templates
Live demo - inventory check agent scenario
Agent-created purchase orders and task architecture
Code units for agent tasks - task builder and message builder
Agent instructions, prompting, and memory management
Agent access control, permissions, and consumption monitoring
Agent debugging, testing, and code-based creation
Agent configuration, KPI tracking, and AL development
Q&A: Sandbox, attachments, multi-agent, and security

features.name: Sales order agent
features.description: Agent that takes emails from customers requesting items, checks inventory, creates quotes, and sends them to customers without human intervention.

features.name: Payables agent
features.description: Agent that processes incoming invoices, captures data, imports information, and posts invoices in the payables process.

features.name: Expense agent
features.description: Agent for handling expense-related tasks that was recently released.
features.status_evidence_quote: now also we have the expense agent that is released recently

features.name: Custom agent creation
features.description: Capability to build custom agents inside Business Central for specific business scenarios, requiring sandbox environment and minimum version 27.4.
features.status_evidence_quote: it is still on on on preview. They are really testing right now from what is happening.

features.name: Agent permissions
features.description: Agents require specific permissions similar to real users, with ability to restrict actions like creating or modifying customers.

features.name: Agent instructions and prompting
features.description: Agents can be configured with instructions that tell them what tasks to perform and steps to take inside Business Central.

features.name: Agent model selection
features.description: Ability to choose the AI model for agent behavior, with current options including Auto, GPT-4.1, and GPT-5.3, with more models to be available from Microsoft.

features.name: Agent testing and execution
features.description: Agents can be tested by executing them step-by-step to validate behavior and configuration.

features.name: Inventory check agent
features.description: Custom agent scenario that processes incoming emails, checks item availability in stock, creates purchase orders when items are unavailable, and sends replies to users.

features.name: Agent audit trail
features.description: All agent actions and steps are logged in an audit trail that can be traced and reviewed, including confirmations and instructions provided by users.

features.name: Agent billing and credits
features.description: Agent actions consume credits from Microsoft billing. Free credits are available but amount is unknown; billing must be set up to prevent agents from getting stuck when credits reach zero.
caveats: agents will not function if credits depleted

features.name: Purchase order creation by agent
features.description: Agent can automatically create purchase orders based on inventory checks. The created purchase order is visible in Business Central and agents' updates trigger notifications.

features.name: Task and task message architecture
features.description: Agent execution is based on tasks and task messages. A task can contain multiple task messages from both the user and the agent. Messages are linked through conversation IDs.

features.name: Agent task builder codeunit
features.description: Codeunit used to initialize and create agent tasks with requirements and messages. Part of the three key codeunits for triggering agents.

features.name: Agent task message builder codeunit
features.description: Codeunit to create task messages from agent tasks. Handles adding or ignoring attachments, setting message external IDs, and other message properties.

features.name: External orchestrator
features.description: A separate component outside Business Central that reads tasks and executes them. Iterates through the environment like a real user and can run tasks in parallel asynchronously.

features.name: Job queue integration for email processing
features.description: Job queue is used to read email boxes and trigger agents. Also used to execute outgoing messages when they are in reviewed status.

features.name: Human-in-loop intervention
features.description: Agents can request assistance from humans or send review requests when they encounter issues like items not found or need human decision.

features.name: Agent memory
features.description: Agent can memorize every single action performed, though not the state. Instructions can tell the agent to keep specific values in memory for later retrieval.
caveats: does not memorize state, only actions
Must be explicitly instructed via prompts

features.name: Agent tools per page type
features.description: Extra tools can be provided to agents through instructions. Different tools are available per page type.
caveats: Tool availability varies by page type

features.name: Page-Specific Instructions
features.description: Agents can have page-specific instructions defined using task tags that execute only when a particular page ID is opened, useful for managing long instruction sets.

features.name: Agent Role Center Limitation
features.description: Agents can be limited by creating a specific role center that restricts which pages they can access. The agent sees only the pages, items, and tiles configured in that role center.

features.name: Page Column Limitation
features.description: Agents can be restricted to see only specific columns in list pages through UI customization, preventing confusion with unnecessary fields.

features.name: Tell Me Search Restriction
features.description: Agents do not have access to the Tell Me search feature and cannot navigate using search instructions, limiting navigation to explicitly configured actions.

features.name: Page Customization with Boolean Flags
features.description: Developers can use page customization to control field visibility for agents, setting fields like quantity to true and location to false to restrict what the agent can see or interact with.

features.name: Agent Permission Model
features.description: Agent permissions are combined with user permissions. When a user approves an agent action through a review dialog, the agent is elevated to the combined permissions of the user and the agent profile for that specific action.

features.name: Agent Consumption Tracking
features.description: Developers can view agent consumption data showing how many credits each action consumes, enabling billing predictions and cost management for customer deployments.

features.name: Agent Task and Subtask Execution
features.description: Each agent task consists of multiple subtasks that can be viewed individually, showing the execution steps performed by the agent with detailed step tracking.

features.name: Agent JSON Representation and Visibility
features.description: Developers can view the JSON representation of pages as the agent sees them, including field names, tool tips, and available tools, enabling debugging of agent perception.
caveats: Includes tool tips but not developer descriptions

features.name: Tool Tips and Error Messages for Agents
features.description: Agents can read tool tips on fields and will read error messages to retry operations. Clear UI design with understandable tool tips and error messages is critical for agent success.
caveats: Agent behavior dependent on message clarity
Tool tips are read, not field descriptions

features.name: Agent Testing in UI
features.description: Developers should test agents by reading instructions, following clicks in the UI as a real user would navigate, ensuring the UI works as expected for agent automation.

features.name: Agent Factory Codeunit
features.description: The Agent Factory codeunit is used to create agents from code in AL, providing methods to set display name, default profile, and other agent configuration properties.

features.name: Agent Beta Data Interface
features.description: The Agent Beta Data interface allows developers to configure page ID, instructions, summary, and other agent properties when creating agents programmatically.

features.name: Agent Configuration Dialogue Page Type
features.description: A new page type for agent configuration that acts as a setup page for guided experience, allowing configuration of settings like email address and message limits per agent.
caveats: Primary key must include user security ID

features.name: Agent Capability Registration
features.description: Agents must register their capabilities with status levels of early preview, preview, or production, and must mark the copilot billing type as build to track credit usage.
caveats: Billing type must always be marked build

features.name: Agent Creation Codeunit with Activate Function
features.description: A codeunit with a create and activate function is used to create agents and set instructions, allowing instruction updates when delivered to customers.
caveats: Instructions must be managed through code unit or key vault
Instructions are critical to agent behavior

features.name: Agent KPI Page
features.description: A KPI page that generates statistics for agents including number of emails received, replies, and tasks created. The table must have user security ID for proper tracking.
caveats: Table must have user security ID
KPI calculation is based on specific metrics

features.name: AL Agent Development
features.description: Agents can be developed using AL language with full Business Central context. AL agents have advantages including full access to pages, limited API exposure needed, use of existing extension distribution infrastructure, and version control.

features.name: Copilot Studio vs AL Agent Comparison
features.description: Copilot Studio provides chat UI but limited to single customer distribution. AL agents integrate with Business Central using full context and pages, requiring no API exposure, with existing app source distribution and version control infrastructure.
caveats: Copilot Studio is single customer focused

features.name: Copilot-AL Agent Interaction
features.description: On the roadmap, copilot agents will be able to interact with AL agents for enhanced orchestration capabilities.
features.status_evidence_quote: later on the road map there will be also that copilot agents can interact with AL agents

features.name: Sandbox-Only Development
features.description: Agent development is currently limited to prototyping on sandbox environments only, with no production availability yet.

features.name: Agent Testing Requirements
features.description: Agents must be tested with multiple variants to ensure correct performance. Testing is required as code, and must be repeated when the model changes.

features.name: Agent Attachment Handling
features.description: Custom integration is required to retrieve and read attachments from email, Azure blob storage, SharePoint or other sources as part of agent tasks.
caveats: Must attach via task message builder

features.name: Single Agent Context Limitation
features.description: Agents are only aware of their own context and cannot directly call other agents. Multi-agent workflows require separate task messages.
caveats: Must use task messages for orchestration

features.name: Prompt Injection Prevention
features.description: Security guards in agent instructions are required to prevent prompt injection attacks. Price modifications and other sensitive operations must be restricted in instructions.
caveats: Meta prompt from Microsoft not visible

features.name: AL Agent Project Template
features.description: Microsoft provides a ready-made template in VS Code through the AL new project agent command in the command palette for starting agent development.
